> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `80311501c02070f72ddae4431403f95e5642aec3` — the merge of head `94604ee51bbdc3c5ba73d147604c4ec7e6e81816` into base `53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 80311501c02070f72ddae4431403f95e5642aec3 && git checkout 80311501c02070f72ddae4431403f95e5642aec3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350 94604ee51bbdc3c5ba73d147604c4ec7e6e81816 && git checkout -B drift-repro 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350 && git merge --no-ff 94604ee51bbdc3c5ba73d147604c4ec7e6e81816

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `94604ee51bbdc3c5ba73d147604c4ec7e6e81816`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23689's body and all six comments (triage 6196324526, claim 6198937330, dispatch 6198975590, Walk reading 6199252355, grade change 6200228776, report 6200333099); PR #23716's body, its four-file list, and the net diff `origin/main...94604ee51` (merge base `69351e985`); the 41 check-runs on this head. In the cited code at the head I read `ObjectQLPlugin.start()`, `followRuntimeObjectCopy`, `settleRuntimeObjectCopy`, `mirrorRuntimeObject` and `putObjectCopy` (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`), the per-engine registry (`engine.ts`), `isTenantAuthored` (`metadata-core`), `MetadataManager.registerInMemory`, `MetadataPlugin`'s service and artifact load, `resolvePluginOrder`, `MCPServerPlugin.start()`, the stdio bridge's `GATED_ACTIONS` note, and PR #23694's `plugin.ts` hunk (`cd86e41b0`). Governing text: AGENTS.md "Add a changeset for anything that publishes" (a fix to a released package is `patch`; `Clause-②: yes|no` plus at most one arm), the spec's `enable.apiEnabled` ("Expose object via automatic APIs"), the `hydrateMetadataFromDb` option docblock, and the dispatch's bound (the producer only; ⛔ `start()`'s boot order and the `objectql:drivers-ready` region).

### ① Derived judgments

- **MCP stdio data verbs on an `apiEnabled: false` runtime-authored object, on an `environmentId` kernel.** `query_records`, `get_record`, `create_record`, `update_record` and `delete_record` were served and are now refused with `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` / 404. **Right.** This is the meaning the spec declares for the key. REST refused the same objects on the same boot, and both MCP doors already refuse them on the no-`environmentId` shape (PR #23687). The implementation now matches the declaration; no published accept set narrows.
- **HTTP MCP data verbs (`refuseUnexposedDataAction`).** The gate answered ALLOWED and now refuses. **Right**, for the same reason: the gate reads the same service, and the fix is at that service's producer. The dispatch ruled out a consumer-side tolerance, and none was added: `packages/mcp` and `packages/runtime` are untouched.
- **`list_objects` / `describe_object`, the `objectstack://objects` resource, AI describe and `metadata.getObject` / `listObjects` on this shape.** Before, these named no runtime-authored object. Now they name and describe every one. **Right.** That is the answer the bridge's own docblock gives the metadata service ("visible to AI tools and other consumers that query IMetadataService"), and it matches the no-`environmentId` shape. One precision the PR body leaves out: the body says "exposed" objects, but the listing and the describe now also cover objects with `apiEnabled: false`. That is schema only, not data. These two reads are deliberately not gated on exposure (the stdio bridge's `GATED_ACTIONS` note), exactly as on the other shape, so this is parity and not a defect.
- **The follow, armed on every `environmentId` kernel, including ones without `hydrateMetadataFromDb`.** It copies only from this engine's own registry (`engine.ts`: a per-engine `_registry`, "so kernels are fully isolated") into this kernel's own service. The trigger is this kernel's own `onMetadataMutation`. It writes through `registerInMemory`. `unregister` stays under the three bounds #23687 set, which this diff does not change: the mutation says `deleted`, the registry no longer serves the name, and the copy is tenant-authored. **Right**: no other environment's rows are reachable. `start()` has an older comment calling `SchemaRegistry` "a process-wide singleton". It is stale, it is not in this diff, and it does not bear on the change.
- **The boot pass (`bridgeRuntimeObjectsToMetadataService`).** It runs only when `environmentId` is set and `hydrateMetadataFromDb` is on. It copies only names whose registry owner row satisfies `isTenantAuthored` (`_provenance === 'org'`). Code-package objects stay out, and a pin covers that (the shipped package's object has no copy, before or after a runtime edit beside it). The write is `registerInMemory`: on `MetadataPlugin`'s `NodeMetadataManager` that is an in-memory map set plus a list-cache invalidation, with no loader write and no announce. The `register(..., { notify: false })` fallback applies only to a service that lacks `registerInMemory`, which this one does not. The rows come from this kernel's own `sys_metadata`, under the option's own contract ("Set this ONLY when the kernel's registry is per-instance isolated AND `sys_metadata` lives on the kernel's own local driver"). **Right**: it copies nothing it must not, and nothing is written through to a loader.
- **A window before the copy exists.** The pass sits on the exact line the full bridge occupies on the other shape: after Phase-2 hydration and Phase-3 sync, before `kernel:ready`. Before hydration, the registry does not hold the object either. In the composed stack, MCP is a capability provider. It is mounted after the stack plugins and declares no dependencies, and `resolvePluginOrder` walks in registration order, so `ObjectQLPlugin.start()` (and with it the copy) runs before MCP's stdio `runtime.start()`. The HTTP MCP door serves only once the listener is open. **Right**: any remaining pre-copy window is the one the no-`environmentId` bridge already has at the same line, not a new one.
- **The boot-copy failure line (`ctx.logger.error`, naming the objects, the consequence and the way out).** This is operator output, not an accept set. **Right.**
- **Public API.** No export, option, type or event is added or removed, and both new members are `private`. The no-`environmentId` behaviour is unchanged: that leg's pins stayed green under both ablations. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

The changeset is `.changeset/23689-env-kernel-runtime-object-copy.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`. Its body carries `Clause-②: no`, and so does the PR body. `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true`, and its file here is a test, so it needs no changeset. **The level matches what the diff publishes.** It is a fix inside a released package, with no new or removed export, option, event or schema key. The contrast is PR #23694: it added `OBJECTQL_DRIVERS_READY_HOOK` and the `objectql:drivers-ready` event, and so declared `yes` and `minor`. Check Changeset concluded `success`.

`Clause-②: no` **holds.** The refusals on both MCP doors return the implementation to `apiEnabled: false`'s declared contract. REST on the same boot already enforced that contract, and so did both doors on the other kernel shape. The listing and describe change restores the metadata service's documented content on this shape, at parity with the other shape. No published contract is narrowed or widened, so neither arm applies. `no (narrowing)` would be wrong, because no declared accept set shrinks.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0]: is the boot copy's `else if` inside the dispatch's bound?** **Yes: A.** The bound is `start()`'s boot order and the `objectql:drivers-ready` region. The new branch moves no step. It is an `else if` on the existing bridge gate, at the bridge's own position. #23694's hunk is one `ctx.trigger('objectql:drivers-ready', ...)` after `ql.init()` and before Phase 1, about fifty lines earlier and disjoint. Since the merge base, `main` has changed `plugin.ts` only by that hunk, and the PR reads `mergeable_state: clean`. The claim's file surface literally said "the copy follow only". The seat's grade change 6200228776 widened that to "copies hydrated runtime-authored objects once at boot on this shape", on the strength of reading (d), so the boot copy is in scope. Option B (`kernel:ready`) would open the window that A avoids.
- **open_questions[1]: is a cloud-side confirmation needed?** **A, with no escalation.** The gates now coincide. Hydration runs when `environmentId === undefined || hydrateMetadataFromDb`, and in exactly those cases a copy follows: the full bridge, or this boot pass. A composition without `hydrateMetadataFromDb` puts no hydrated runtime object in the registry, so no door serves one. The mutation follow covers saves on every shape. The dev's conditional B therefore guards no case this diff leaves open. A cloud-lane walk stays the cloud lane's own choice and does not gate this PR.
- **open_questions[2]: `Clause-②`.** **A, `no`.** See ②.
- **open_questions[3]: the primary checkout was detached to create the worktree.** Noted. This is process only; it touches nothing in the diff.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0].** The HTTP door's refusal carries no error code. #23528 already tracks it, so this is correctly not filed.
- **out_of_scope_findings[1], and the acceptance notes.** The stdio leg ran in-process over `createStandaloneStack`'s plugin options rather than through a spawned `os dev`, and the cloud host was not booted. Both are accepted, since the in-repo shape is the one the `hydrateMetadataFromDb` docblock names. The door pin `mcp-stdio-runtime-object-exposure.test.ts` belongs to the dogfood suite. That suite runs only in the full battery (`ci.yml`, "THE TWO SPEEDS"), so the dogfood shards were skipped on this head. For the PR, its evidence is the dev's local 10-of-10 run and the mutant-`dist` ablation (5 red on the `environmentId` shape, 5 green on the CONTROL shape). It runs on `main`'s full battery after merge. The producer pins in `plugin-runtime-object-metadata-copy.test.ts` ran in Test Core.
- **CI on this head.** 41 check-runs, all completed: 35 `success`, 6 `skipped`, none failed or pending. The skipped six are Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, the Dogfood Regression Gate shard matrix (full-battery only), and Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in). Test Core (all six shards), Build Core, every Type Check and Lint job, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, both single-claim guards and the card-claims-branch check are all `success`.

Implemented-by: `session_01QBn4EzKV17Y1Ero6KDNZ45`
Reviewed-by: `session_01GP3comALHRcRBixS2TEnLF`

**VERDICT: PASS**
